target_customer: Engineering and operations teams at companies that build and run AI agents and workflows, plus individual developers using the open source project
problem: Building reliable AI agent workflows required boilerplate code and opaque framework abstractions. Sim offers a visual canvas where the workflow is explicit.
business_model: Open source core with hosted freemium tiers (Free, Pro, Max, Enterprise); prices not shown on the site
product_category: AI agent workflow builder and workspace

founders.name: Emir Karabeg
education: UC Berkeley, Data Science and Cognitive Science
previous_startups: WorkNinja (AI learning platform, 300,000+ MAU per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Did NLP research on machine translation at Berkeley per YC page.

founders.name: Waleed Latif
education: UC Berkeley, CS and Cognitive Science

competitors.name: n8n
competitors.what: Workflow automation with AI nodes, source available under a Sustainable Use License
competitors.traction_then: Named by the founders as the main comparison in the April 2025 Show HN thread; no figures in the source

technical_complexity.rationale: A visual canvas executing multi-agent graphs, integrations and a hosted runtime is standard product engineering with some hard parts, built by two engineers in early 2025.

defensibility.rationale: Apache 2.0 licence means code can be forked, and n8n, Flowise and others already offered visual builders. Integration breadth and a community are the main edges.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: By 2026 the company repositioned as an AI workspace with a conversational layer (Mothership, March 2026); no acquisition reported as of the sources found.

market_need_then: Spring 2025 saw rapid interest in agent builders; the founders cited frustration with boilerplate-heavy frameworks, and the open source repo attracted thousands of GitHub stars within months.

branding.domain_note: Launched as Sim Studio; later used sim.ai, date of domain acquisition not found.

identity.logo: Simple wordmark; description not found in sources
identity.visual_style: Minimal product-led canvas UI; a design agency case study exists (Hex)

branding.community_and_virality: Open source repo with roughly 18,000 GitHub stars by Nov 2025 per press and about 28,000 to 30,000 per later directories; Show HN in April 2025 and Launch HN in May 2025.

brand_strength.rationale: Open source community and GitHub traction drove awareness, but the one-syllable generic name is confusable with Simplif-type names and other Sim companies.

pivots.to: AI workspace with conversational control plane (Mothership)
pivots.why: Product expansion described in coverage; not a change of market

outcome_analysis: Sim grew from an April 2025 Show HN open source launch to a $7M Series A in November 2025 led by Standard Capital, with company reported adoption of about 60,000 developers and over 100 production companies. The open source distribution and the agent boom helped it, while the forkable licence and crowded visual builder market remain risks. It is active with no exit.
notes: Batch labeled X25 by some sources and P25 by others; the directory says Spring 2025. Series A seen in StartupHub (opened) and Pulse 2.0 (snippet) and EveryDev listing. A $500K pre-seed appears only in aggregators (Employbl, EveryDev) and is unverified, so not recorded as a round. Traction figures are company reported. No outcome events (acquisition, layoffs) found.
